title: Texas's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for Texas's 6th Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, pitting Republican incumbent Jake Ellzey against Democratic nominee Danny Minton. Ellzey, first elected in a 2021 special election, won his primary challenge with 66.3% of the vote against two challengers. Minton ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination. The district covers portions of Dallas, Tarrant, Ellis, Johnson, and Navarro counties in the Dallas-Fort Worth region. Mid-decade redistricting in 2025 redrew the district's boundaries, a move that was challenged in federal court as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander but ultimately allowed by the Supreme Court. The Cook Political Report rates this race as 'Solid Republican.'
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the Texas's 6th Congressional District general election were found in available sources.

candidates.name: Jake Ellzey
candidates.summary: Jake Ellzey is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 6th Congressional District, first elected in a 2021 special election. A former U.S. Navy fighter pilot who served 20 years and achieved the rank of Commander, Ellzey also served briefly in the Texas House of Representatives and on the Texas Veterans Commission. He won the Republican primary on March 3, 2026 with 66.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: Danny Minton
candidates.summary: Danny Minton is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 6th Congressional District, having run unopposed in the March 3, 2026 primary. A healthcare industry professional working in breast cancer surgical technology sales, Minton holds a BS in Zoology from the University of Oklahoma with advanced studies in epidemiology. He is a former Republican who switched parties and has never previously held elected office. Minton lives in Arlington with his wife, a veterinarian, and their two sons.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general election polling exists. This forecast relies entirely on non-polling indicators. Jake Ellzey is the Republican incumbent, first elected in a 2021 special election, who won renomination comfortably (66.3% in the March 2026 primary). Democratic nominee Danny Minton is a first-time candidate who ran unopposed for his party's nomination. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid Republican.' Mid-decade 2025 redistricting—upheld by the Supreme Court after a racial gerrymander challenge—introduces some uncertainty about the district's exact partisan composition, but with no polling, no signs of Democratic strength, and a strong incumbent, the evidence points to a substantial Republican advantage.
